subject: MSA / Order Form: telemetry & training carveouts — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <ops@novara.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hsu <legal@novara.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial redlines — output ownership, telemetry, training carveouts

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the call this morning — attaching Novara's redlines for the MSA and order form (see Novara_Redlines_v1.docx). Main asks are short:

- Novara retains exclusive ownership of any Customer Output and derived product features (we need explicit assignment language in the Order Form).
- No training on Customer Data or Customer Output without an opt-in checkbox and 30-day notice.
- Telemetry/usage logs: Novara will allow anonymized, aggregated telemetry for service improvement only, but we want strict controls and deletion windows (45 days) and a carveout for PII or business-sensitive events.
- Feedback license: Novara will provide non-confidential feedback to Redwood; they will not grant a perpetual training license to productize the feedback beyond operational fixes.

Can you confirm Redwood's prefered fallback language? We flagged the most sensitive sections in the doc. Also attaching a short SOC2 evidence request (Novara-SOC2_ask.pdf) that legal/procurement will expect during vendor review.

Appreciate a short summary of acceptable compromise language so Novara's legal can redline back.

Best,
Elena Cruz
Head of Ops, Novara Systems
ops@novara.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cruz <ops@novara.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial redlines — output ownership, telemetry, training carveouts

Elena — thanks, received the doc and SOC2 checklist.

On Mon, Aug 23, 2026 at 9:12 AM Elena Cruz <ops@novara.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the call this morning — attaching Novara's redlines for the MSA and order form...

High-level response / proposed compromise from Redwood:

- Output ownership: we can accept customer ownership of Customer Output (Order Form exhibit) but need a narrow operational license to host, cache, and deliver that output back to Novara's users (service delivery). We propose explicit language: non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to operate the service and provide the output to Novara end users.

- Training on Customer Data / Output: Redwood does not train general models on customer-provided data by default. We can add an opt-in mechanism: customer may opt-in per model/period; otherwise training is prohibited. For customer-provided feedback (bug reports, anonymized usage patterns) we propose a separate limited feedback license (90 days to use for model tuning improvements limited to internal service quality), not for resale or productization.

- Telemetry: agreeable to aggregated/anonymized telemetry for improvements. We propose a 90-day retention window for aggregated logs used in analytics; raw request logs with potential PII will be kept only for 14 days unless Novara requests extended retention for troubleshooting (case-by-case, documented). We will add a contractual representation around pseudonymization/anonymization practices.

Next steps for us:
- Laura/legal to prepare redline with exact clauses (Operational License wording, opt-in checkbox language, telemetry retention table).
- Jordan to map how the opt-in flag will be surfaced in the Console (API param + UI checkbox).

Laura / Jordan — can you draft the short redline (Order Form exhibit + MSA clause) by EOD tomorrow? Elena — if acceptable, we'll circulate a targeted redline and ask Novara's legal to confirm.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Tom Hsu <legal@novara.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <ops@novara.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T14:48:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial redlines — output ownership, telemetry, training carveouts

Kimberly / Elena — thanks for the quick reply and the proposed structure. A couple of clarifying asks from Novara legal before we take a formal redline: 

- Please confirm the exact wording for the "operational license" (we need to see whether it includes a right to cache, replicate, or otherwise persist Customer Output outside of ephemeral runtime).
- The feedback license timeframe (90 days) is better than perpetual, but Novara will insist on a hard constraint preventing use of Customer Output-derived examples in model releases or commercial features.
- Telemetry: 90-day aggregated retention still makes Novara nervous. Would Redwood consider 45 days for aggregated telemetry and 14 days for non-aggregated request-level logs, with an exception workflow for troubleshooting?

Proposed compromise language (for your internal counsel to shape):

- Customer retains title to Customer Output. Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to store and serve Customer Output solely to provide the Services defined in the Order Form. Storage beyond 30 days requires documented approval.
- Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Output to train foundation models absent an explicit written opt-in per product and per dataset. Feedback (non-PII, aggregated metrics) may be used for service-quality tuning for up to 90 days but may not be included in models intended for general release or resale.
- Telemetry will be collected only as necessary and pseudonymized; request-level logs will be retained 14 days by default and aggregated metrics 45 days. Any request for extended retention requires Novara approval and an audit trail.

We can accept a limited operational license as described if Redwood can: (1) add the 30-day storage cap option, and (2) commit to an explicit training opt-in workflow.

If Redwood legal can provide working redlines with the proposed wording (or close variants), Novara legal will review and aim to return a clean set within 48 hours.

Regards,
Tom Hsu
Senior Counsel, Novara Systems
legal@novara.com

Attachment: Novara_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

Kim / Jordan — drafting complete. Summary of edits added to the redline (attached to mailbox):

- Order Form exhibit: explicit Customer Output assignment clause + operational license paragraph (we used the non-exclusive / non-sublicensable wording and added an explicit "serve & cache for up to 30 days" sentence).
- MSA: added training prohibition except by written opt-in; added definition for "Feedback" and limited feedback license to 90 days for internal service tuning only.
- Telemetry table: request-level logs 14 days; aggregated metrics 45 days by default; documented exception flow for troubleshooting.

I uploaded the draft to HubSpot and included the DocuSign placeholder (link in related_links). Jordan — we need a one-paragraph help text for the Console opt-in that we can paste into the Order Form UI.

Elena/Tom — we'll send this as a narrow redline. Kimberly, want me to send or do you prefer to review first?
